Tagline: Wait for a walk-in clinic from home, not the waiting room.
About The Project:
At walk-in clinics people can wait two hours in a crowded room. Clinic Queue lets patients join the queue by text message and texts them when they're about 15 minutes from being seen. No app or smartphone is needed, which matters because many patients at community clinics don't have mobile data.

A volunteer receptionist at a community clinic gave us feedback on Saturday morning: the receptionist view needed to be one screen with big buttons, so we rebuilt it. The full flow works end to end with real texts: join, position updates, 'you're next' and 'missed your turn'. We tested it with eight people on their own phones while the receptionist screen ran on a laptop.

Tagline: Feedback on the structure of your essay, not just the spelling.
About The Project:
🏆 Update: we won 2nd place overall, thank you to the judges!
Draft Buddy is a Chrome extension for Google Docs that gives feedback on an essay's structure: whether each paragraph makes one point, whether the introduction matches the conclusion, and where evidence is missing. It uses a large language model, with a prompt we refined on ten real essays from our course (shared with permission).

It deliberately doesn't rewrite anything for you, because our lecturers said that would count as academic misconduct. The extension works in Docs today, and feedback takes about eight seconds per essay.
Built With: JavaScript, Chrome Extensions API, OpenAI API

Tagline: Point your camera at a menu and see what you can't eat.
About The Project: People with allergies have to ask about every dish. Allergen Alert reads a photo of a menu with OCR and highlights dishes that probably contain your allergens. The OCR works on printed menus but struggles with handwritten specials boards. Allergen detection is a keyword list, so it catches 'peanut' but misses dishes like satay unless the menu says so. It won't replace asking the staff, and the app says so. We'd like to train a proper model.
Sponsor Prizes: Best Social Impact, Best Use of Data

Tagline: Match volunteers' spare hours to what local charities actually need.
About The Project:
Small charities told us they get plenty of offers of help but can't match them to real tasks. Volunteer Match lets a charity post a specific task with a skill and a time slot (for example 'two hours on Saturday setting up a food bank'), and volunteers are matched by skills and availability.

We built the charity task form, the volunteer profile and the matching. We emailed three local charities on Friday; one food bank coordinator replied with four real tasks, which are in our demo. Matching is a simple score on skills and time overlap, which we think is easier to trust than a black box.

Tagline: Turn your workout notes into progress charts.
About The Project: Lots of people log workouts in their phone's notes app. We built Gym Graph because we kept forgetting what we'd lifted in the first place. It parses notes like 'bench 3x8 60kg' into structured data and charts progress for each exercise. The parser handles the formats we use and breaks on unusual ones. Charts work for strength exercises but not cardio yet.

Tagline: Is that flat overpriced? Check it against what similar flats really rent for.
About The Project:
Students often sign leases without knowing whether the rent is fair. Rent Radar compares a listing's rent with similar properties, using an open dataset of 41,000 registered tenancies (rent, bedrooms, area and property type).

We trained a gradient-boosted model to predict rent from those features. On a held-out 20% of the data its median error is £58 a month, compared with £131 for simply using the area's average, and we show an uncertainty range rather than a single number. It knows nothing about condition or furnishing, and the result page says so clearly.

Tagline: A puzzle game that teaches children loops and conditions.
About The Project: All four of us are first-years and this is our first hackathon. Code Quest is a browser game where children guide a robot through a maze by snapping together instruction blocks like 'move', 'turn' and 'repeat'. Levels 1 to 3 work, and level 3 introduces loops. We tested it with a teammate's 9-year-old cousin over a video call: she finished all three levels in 12 minutes but got stuck on the repeat block, so we added a hint.

Tagline: Your revolutionary AI companion for mental health, available 24/7.
About The Project:
Mental health is a crisis, with millions of people unable to access therapy. MindMate AI is a revolutionary AI companion that will provide personalised mental health support to anyone, anywhere, at any time, replacing long waiting lists with instant care.

MindMate uses cutting-edge large language models to understand your emotions, diagnose conditions like anxiety and depression, and deliver tailored cognitive behavioural therapy. Our proprietary algorithm learns from every conversation and becomes more accurate over time. We believe MindMate is more empathetic than human therapists because it never gets tired.

In the future MindMate will integrate with wearables to detect mood changes before you notice them, connect to health services, and offer a premium tier with daily coaching. We will also build a marketplace for wellness products.

During the hackathon we built a chat interface where you can talk to MindMate, connected to a language model with a system prompt telling it to act as a therapist. It works well in our testing and users love it. Our next steps are clinical validation and raising seed funding.

Tagline: A simple board for lost property on campus.
About The Project: Post something you found, or search for something you lost. We built a basic web app with posting and search.

Tagline: Compare journeys by carbon as well as time.
About The Project: EcoRoute shows the same journey by bus, train, bike and car, with estimated travel time and CO2 for each, using public routing APIs and published emissions factors per kilometre. It works for any two addresses in the UK. We found that for most journeys under 5 km, cycling was within ten minutes of driving. We haven't tested it with users yet.

Tagline: Practise British Sign Language fingerspelling with instant feedback from your webcam.
About The Project:
Sign Snap uses your webcam to check whether you're forming British Sign Language fingerspelling letters correctly. We trained a small classifier on hand landmarks from MediaPipe, using about 1,200 images we recorded ourselves during the hackathon.

It recognises five letters so far (A, B, C, L and O). On images of a teammate who wasn't in the training data it got 41 of 50 right (82%), though it confuses C and O. A member of a Deaf student society told us fingerspelling is what beginners find hardest to get feedback on.
Sponsor Prizes: Best Social Impact, Best Use of Data

Tagline: A week of meals for under £25.
About The Project: Budget Bites plans a week of meals on a student budget. You set a budget and any dietary needs, and it builds a meal plan and shopping list from supermarket prices we collected by hand for 120 common ingredients. The plan and the list work. Prices will go out of date, which a supermarket API would fix. There's also a 'cook once, eat twice' mode.
